description.narrative: The development objective of the Integrated Disaster Resilience Program-for-Results Project for Tunisia is to strengthen Tunisia's disaster risk management and financing, and to enhance the protection of the targeted population and assets from disaster and climate-related events. The program is structured around four result areas (RAs). The first RA, improving flood risk reduction will support the Government of Tunisia (GoT) in its efforts to improve flood risk reduction in urban areas. This will be achieved through physical investments in urban flood risk reduction projects. The second RA, enhanced disaster preparedness will support the GoT in strengthening disaster preparedness. The third RA, strengthening financial protection will support the GoT in strengthening its financial protection capacity. The fourth RA, promoting institutional coordination and a sound regulatory environment for climate and disaster risk management will promote institutional coordination and a sound regulatory environment for climate and disaster risk management.
To strenghten Tunisia's disaster risk management and financing, and to enhance the protection of the targeted population and assets from disaster and climate-related events.

title.narrative: An improved understanding of catastrophic risk and a developed actuarial model allowing the increase of the coverage of Nat Cat insurance.

baseline.value: No catastrophic risk data base and no actuarial model.

target.value: Dissemination of the insights coming from the finalized actuarial model and from the financial exposure database updates to the insurance sector.

actual.value: A catastrophic risk database and no actuarial model.

title.narrative: Organizational and institutional reform of the climate and hydrometeorological service providers in place.

baseline.value: - Laws establishing the INM and the MARHP but no regulatory text exists to establish the hydromet value chain- INM organizational chart proposal, but not yet approved- No data sharing protocol except the agreement for Medjerda. Recently signed INM-MinAgri general agreement

target.value: Regulations for data exchange adopted the Ministries concerned.

actual.value: - The bid for the development of data exchange protocols throughout the HydroMet value chain and related regulatory text has been unsuccessful and is awaiting re-adverstising (expected in July 2023).- New INM organizational chart has not been approved yet but is expected to be approved by the end of 2023.

title.narrative: Urban flood risk reduction projects are implemented and completed.

target.value: (i)Cumulative value of works implemented to date of flood risk reduction investment projects is TDM 112(ii) Cumulative number of completed flood risk reduction projects is 6.

title.narrative: Number of eligible beneficiaries of a public financing mechanism in line with the priorities and objectives set in the National DRF strategy, with a monitoring of the share of women beneficiaries.
Number of people reached by Multi-Hazards Impact-Based Forecasts and Early Warning Services - disaggregated by sex.
Number of people covered by urban flood risk reduction infrastructure supported by the Program - disaggregated by sex
A sovereign disaster risk financing (DRF) Strategy is implemented.

baseline.value: Absence of a National DRF strategy.

target.value: Operationalization of the public financing mechanism and of the national compensation (claims) registry that collects disaggregated data on women's and men's coverage in case of disasters.

actual.value: Absence of a National DRF strategy.

title.narrative: Institutional coordination mechanisms and the regulatory framework for climate and disaster risk management are strengthened.

baseline.value: Absence of an updated and integrated legal framework covering all DRM components. Existence of a 1991 Law focusing on emergency preparedness and response and establishing the National Commission and Regional Commissions for the Fight Against Calamities. Existence of a 2018 Local Government code transferring DRM-related responsibilities to municipalities.

target.value: An action plan to continue the regulatory and institutional reforminitiated through the Program, outlining the new institutional framework and roles and responsibilities and policy priorities to strengthen sustainable climate resilience and disaster risk management in Tunisia has been approved by the Borrower.

actual.value: Final draft of the decree establishing the SPR was finalized by Pillar V working group, and circulated for approval of the Council of Ministers.

title.narrative: Production and implementation of MH-IBF-EWS, with emphasis on climate-related events (e.g floods).

baseline.value: - The first version of the 'Carte de Vigilanceâ€™ exists- National weather forecasts exist, but need to be brought down to regional and local levels- Hydrological modeling only for Medjerda.

target.value: The improved â€˜Carte de Vigilanceâ€™ including Vigicrue and the impact-based forecasts and risk-based warnings are rolled out nationally.

actual.value: - The meteorological "Carte de Vigilance" has been extended with additional hazards (heatwaves).- Two bids were unsuccessful and awaiting to be relaunched in July 2023. Eight bidding documents have been prepared and are awaiting publication by the end of 2023. Technical support has been provided on the bidding process for the weather radars and capacity building is expected to be delivered through WB TA as soon as S2 2023. One activity was adjusted for the membership to the ECMWF instead of the purchase of license (ongoing); WB TA will support the delivery of the activity on numerical weather prediction as of S2 2023. These processes are supporting the implementation of 10 activities required to improve monitoring systems that are part of the MH-IBF-EWS.

title.narrative: The early warning systems in the country are strengthened.

baseline.value: Absence of a national and regional levels early warning systems.

target.value: Establishment of early response plans at the national, regional and local level in pilot areas, EWS communication strategy.

actual.value: - Few elements of the EWS implemented with the support of other development partners. - Terms of Reference for an EWS Committee/Working Group have been drafted, but further discussions are required for finalization.

title.narrative: Enhanced business opportunities by developing products targeting selected sectors.

baseline.value: No products and services dedicated to sectors (except meteorological products and services for aviation).

target.value: Commercial products developed for the Agriculture sector tested and adopted.

actual.value: No products and services are dedicated to sectors (except meteorological products and services for aviation). Bidding documents for the preparation of the Service Delivery Strategy and Action Plan and for Quality Management Systems have been prepared and advertisd in August 2022; an output of this strategy includes the definition of the products for the Transport and Agriculture sectors.
